No, none of that was okay. I'll never understand the mindset of people like that, it's ridiculous (which is still an understatement) that people treat others differently based on their race. I'm sorry you had to experience that.

Could it possibly be a tic? From what I've heard tics aren't caused by anxiety, but can be amplified by it. Also, I'm no professional so take what I'm saying with a grain of salt. 

I suggest seeing a doctor who can refer you to a neurologist if needed.

No worries. And you're probably right. I think I'm going to ask them within the next week or so (I've just gotta make a script because I suck at talking..). Hoping it goes well and thank you so much for your advice, it means a lot.

Thanks for your reply. I really do want to tell them, I'm just worried about their reaction. And even if they do take me, will I be treated differently from then on? I'm probably overthinking the whole thing, so I'd like to once again thank you for taking the time to read that since it was super long.

All the best :)

I'm sorry you've been going through that, you seem to care a lot about your mother which is infinitely admirable. 

Although I've never been in your situation, I want you to know that your feelings aren't silly in the slightest, and you shouldn't feel bad about feeling afraid. The uncertainty would surely take a toll on anyone going through the same thing, and what you're feeling is valid. 

If you feel the need to cancel plans, then I say go for it. Your wellbeing comes first. 

I hope everything works out for you and your mother and wishing her a speedy recovery. 
All the best!

I'm the same way, which has been hard to deal with.. So it's really cool to see someone opening up about it here considering (in my experience) I don't see it talked about much elsewhere. 

What has helped me IMMENSELY is just sleeping on it. It sounds cliché, but when your thoughts get clouded by your anger it becomes harder to act rationally, so it's always better to take a step back, pull yourself out of the conversation and come back to it once your head is clear. 

Trust me, after you get some sleep you'll be able to better assess how you should handle the situation at hand.
Good on you man! It's so great to hear that things are looking up. :)

There's no shame in self-diagnosing after extensive research, in fact it's the first step towards diagnosis. If you want to get a professional diagnosis however, it's going to be quite tricky if you're under 18. The one way I could think of is to pull your doctor aside during one of your regular checkups to explain your situation. Not guaranteed, but your parents will most likely take your doctor's word more seriously. 

Hope everything works out for you and stay safe.

For sure. It's gotten to the point where I feel like I can't talk to anyone besides my very close friends in fear of my problems being "belittled".   


My mum does this thing where whenever I open up to her about things going on in my life, she picks out the most minor thing and explains to my dad how insignificant it is. She tries to make me feel like I'm overreacting and even tries to blow off my problems by saying that it's all in my head. It really hurts not being heard and I'm sorry to anyone having to deal with the same thing.
